findings.evidence: Scratch probe /tmp/vgoal/u1/scratch-cr-1 (throwaway vitest file, removed): root dep app-tool@1.0.0 -> native-bin ^1.0.0; native-bin 1.0.0/1.1.0 with cpu:["x64"]. HEAD code: no override -> 'THROW ENATIVEUNSUPPORTED'; rifty 'native-bin@1.0.0' -> 'OK node_modules/native-bin 1.0.0' (pre-existing ADR-0051 'overrides exempt'); npm '1.0.0' -> 'Failed to fetch packument 1.0.0: 404'. With a minimal ADR-0451 decision-5 parse spike (overrides.ts + $ admission; all 48 RED tests green): npm '1.0.0' -> 'OK node_modules/native-bin 1.0.0', '^1.0.0' -> 'OK node_modules/native-bin 1.1.0' — no ENATIVEUNSUPPORTED. Gate: installer-sources.ts:214 and :448 `if (!override) assertNativeSupported(...)`.
findings.summary: ADR-0451's {name: N, range: V} user override is non-null, so ADR-0051's `!override` native gate (installer-sources.ts:214 replay, :448 live) is skipped: every npm-authored version/range pin of a cpu-pinned native package will install the binary silently instead of loud ENATIVEUNSUPPORTED. Contract Decisions ('parse-only … no mechanism changes') and ADR-0451 §Divergences neither record nor decide this; decide (keep the gate for same-name overrides, or record + compat) with a RED before Final+GREEN.

Decision 5's grammar is handwritten (semver rejected) and pinned only by the 30-value classify corpus; npm-valid spellings outside it (spaced operators `>= 8.0.0`, `1.x.x`, `~1`, `^0.0.x`, `8.0.0 - 9`, `<8.0.0-rc.1`, build metadata) are unproven, so a predicate that misreads them as names passes every RED. Cheap to widen: the probe is deterministic.

findings.evidence: Golden registryFacts (reproduced byte-identical): decoys {"2":"3.0.0","x":"0.1.2","latest":"0.2.0","beta":"0.0.1"}; ms dist-tags latest/beta/canary/nightly; npm 'tag-beta' row locks ms 3.0.0-beta.2.
findings.summary: Dist-tag words other than `latest` (`beta`, `next`, `canary`) stay rifty replacement names: where the dependent's edge admits the look-alike package's version (e.g. `*`/`latest` edges), rifty installs an unrelated registry package where npm installs the tagged version. Recorded as a divergence, not loud; a dist-tag check against the overridden packument or a named throw would close it.
